mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month indicates an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% over a 3-month period signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening monetary policy coinciding with a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high housing starts (HOUST) and strong GDP growth (GDPC1)), the S&P 500 tends to underperform in the next 60 days due to overvaluation and the expectation of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1750 and GDPC1 > 11400, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0 (index 2017=100) over the past month signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 110.0, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1800 thousand units in a month, it signals strong residential construction activity that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1800, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform in the next 60 days due to reduced consumer spending and lower corporate profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 205.0 (index 1982-1984=100) in a month signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 205.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.
